acceptedAnswer.text: No. Nothing in it models demand, fits a seasonality curve or works out safety stock, and nothing predicts next month. VOS is the ordering front door plus a current picture of stock. We say this first because the word in your search points somewhere we deliberately do not go.

@graph.name: Then why would a distributor shopping for forecasting talk to you?

acceptedAnswer.text: Often the reason a forecast is wrong is what went into it. Phone orders retyped a day late, and invoices standing in for demand. Fix the capture and the tool you already own has something better to read.

@graph.name: What exactly would the planning tool get?

acceptedAnswer.text: For anything sent through the app: the account, the items against your own codes, the quantities as the buyer confirmed them, a reference number and the time it was sent. Inventory forecasting software reading that gets demand, dated at the hour, rather than a shipping summary.

@graph.name: What is the best inventory forecasting software to pair this with?

acceptedAnswer.text: We do not rank them and we name no products, partly because the right answer depends on what your ERP already includes. A planning module you are already paying for may become usable once the order data stops being typed in by hand.

@graph.name: Is any of this inventory forecasting software free?

acceptedAnswer.text: Nothing on this page is a forecasting product, free or paid. VOS itself is quoted per distributor and we publish no prices, so the answer is to ask on the demo call. If a no-cost forecasting tool is what you need, that is not something we sell.

@graph.name: Can we buy AI based inventory forecasting software from you?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. VOS uses no artificial intelligence to project demand and makes no claims of that kind. Voice is used to capture what a person says, and that person reviews every line before sending. Prediction is not part of the product.

@graph.name: We need inventory forecasting software for multinational forecasts. Is this it?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, on two counts. VOS does not forecast, and it is built for smaller food distributors and DSD operations rather than global supply chains. Multi-country planning, currencies and transfer flows are outside what we do.

@graph.name: Where do the stock levels in VOS come from?

acceptedAnswer.text: From whatever you count stock in today. VOS is not where your stock is recorded and it does not count anything on a shelf; it runs alongside what you have, with the catalog updating as levels change. On the demo we walk through how that connection would work for you.
